title: Hair follicle transplantation for hard to heal wounds: Non invasive asessment of skin regeneration
summary:
Chronic wounds, which are often difficult to heal, represent a major challenge in medicine. Our research investigates an innovative approach where hair follicles are transplanted from healthy skin into the wound site. These hair follicles are not only important for hair growth but also introduce special cells (including stem cells) into the wound, which promote healing. Furthermore, hair follicles have an anti-inflammatory effect and can thus reduce chronic inflammation in the wound.

We have observed that the skin regenerating directly around the transplanted hair follicles shows significantly better quality compared to skin that heals conventionally at the wound edge. The hair follicle-induced skin is less dry, shows no scaling, and closely resembles healthy skin. In contrast, the "normally" healed skin at the wound periphery is often dry, scaly, and can appear thin or scarred.

The aim of our study is to non-invasively investigate this outstanding quality of skin created by hair follicle transplantation and to compare it in detail with secondarily healed skin. For this purpose, we use specialized skin measurement devices and high-resolution microscopy (confocal microscopy), which allows us to examine the skin structure at a cellular level without needing to take biopsies.

The insights gained from this work are intended to deepen the understanding of wound healing and to improve future treatment methods for chronic wounds, enabling patients to achieve higher quality and more stable skin regeneration.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients will be included who have been treated with hair follicle transplantations due to chronic wounds and in whom re-epithelialization with complete wound closure has already occurred. Additionally, patients must be medically stable enough to attend outpatient examination appointments. As this involves an investigation of the skin quality of former wound sites after a very specific therapy in a small patient collective, there will be no selection based on age or gender.
Exclusion criteria:
The study participation will be terminated under clearly defined circumstances to ensure the safety of the subjects and the integrity of the study results. Discontinuation occurs if there is a new wound opening or complications at the examined site that make meaningful data collection impossible. Likewise, amputation of the affected skin area during the course of the study leads to the exclusion of the respective person from further analysis. Furthermore, study discontinuation is planned if new severe illnesses or health limitations arise, or if the participant's health condition deteriorates to such an extent that further participation becomes unreasonable or significantly influences the study course
